name: Grove OLED Display 0.96" (SSD1315)
description: 0.96-inch monochrome 128x64 OLED driven by a Solomon Systech SSD1315 controller (SSD1306 command set, internal charge pump enabled with 8Dh 14h). The Grove board has a 3.3 V regulator, an I2C level shifter with 4.7 kΩ pull-ups and a power-on reset circuit, so it runs on 3.3-5 V. I2C address 0x3C (0x3D with the address jumper on 0x7A). Sold as: Seeed Grove - OLED Display 0.96" (SSD1315), 4-pin Grove connector SCL, SDA, VCC, GND, I2C address 0x3C.
eli5: A small screen on a Grove plug that shows text and pictures as glowing white dots.

pins.name: SCL
pins.description: I2C clock (Grove pin 1, yellow wire); level shifted, 4.7 kΩ pull-up on the board.

pins.name: SDA
pins.description: I2C data (Grove pin 2, white wire); level shifted, 4.7 kΩ pull-up on the board.

supplierQuery: Seeed Grove OLED Display 0.96 SSD1315 I2C
buildNotes: Grove connector order (Seeed schematic J1, and printed on the board): pin 1 SCL (yellow), pin 2 SDA (white), pin 3 VCC (red), pin 4 GND (black). The board has a 2 mm Grove socket: use a Grove-to-female-jumper cable to reach the breadboard.
Address jumper on the back: 0x78 position = 7-bit 0x3C (default), 0x7A = 0x3D.
SDA/SCL go through an on-board MOSFET level shifter with 4.7 kΩ pull-ups on both sides, so no external pull-ups are needed and it is safe on 3.3 V or 5 V boards.
The SSD1315 makes its panel voltage with an internal charge pump: send 8Dh 14h before AFh (display on), and allow 100 ms for the panel to come on.
About 25-32 mA with the whole screen white (datasheet IBAT), much less showing text.

driver.code:
# Seeed Grove - OLED Display 0.96" (SSD1315, 128x64, I2C), MicroPython driver.
# Written from the Solomon Systech SSD1315 datasheet (sections 6.2 I2C interface, 6.9.2 power-on
# sequence with charge pump, 6.10 charge pump regulator) and the panel maker's init code for the
# 0.96" SSD1315 module Seeed uses (internal charge pump, 8Dh 14h). The SSD1315 keeps the SSD1306
# command set. I2C: control byte 0x00 = command stream (Co=0, D/C#=0), 0x40 = GDDRAM data stream.
# The Grove board has its own power-on reset circuit (R5/C5/D1), so no RES# pin is needed.
import framebuf
import time


class SSD1315_I2C(framebuf.FrameBuffer):
    def __init__(self, i2c, addr=0x3C, width=128, height=64):
        self.i2c = i2c
        self.addr = addr  # 0x3C (jumper "0x78", default) or 0x3D (jumper "0x7A")
        self.width = width
        self.height = height
        self.pages = height // 8
        self.buffer = bytearray(self.pages * width)
        super().__init__(self.buffer, width, height, framebuf.MONO_VLSB)
        time.sleep_ms(20)   # datasheet 6.9.2: wait >= 20 ms after VDD is stable (board RC reset)
        self.init_display()

    def cmd(self, *b):
        self.i2c.writeto(self.addr, bytes((0x00,) + b))

    def init_display(self):
        self.cmd(0xAE)                   # display off
        self.cmd(0xD5, 0x80)             # clock divide ratio / oscillator frequency
        self.cmd(0xA8, self.height - 1)  # multiplex ratio: 63 for 64 rows
        self.cmd(0xD3, 0x00)             # display offset 0
        self.cmd(0x40)                   # display start line 0
        self.cmd(0x20, 0x00)             # horizontal addressing mode
        self.cmd(0xA1)                   # segment remap: column 127 -> SEG0
        self.cmd(0xC8)                   # COM scan COM[N-1] -> COM0
        self.cmd(0xDA, 0x12)             # alternative COM pin configuration (128x64)
        self.cmd(0x81, 0x7F)             # contrast
        self.cmd(0xD9, 0x22)             # pre-charge period (module maker's value)
        self.cmd(0xDB, 0x30)             # VCOMH deselect level (module maker's value)
        self.cmd(0xA4)                   # display follows RAM
        self.cmd(0xA6)                   # normal (not inverted)
        self.cmd(0x8D, 0x14)             # enable internal charge pump (VBAT = 3.3 V on the board)
        self.fill(0)
        self.show()
        self.cmd(0xAF)                   # display on
        time.sleep_ms(100)               # SEG/COM turn on 100 ms after AFh (tAF)

    def poweroff(self):
        self.cmd(0xAE)                   # display off, then charge pump off (power-off sequence)
        self.cmd(0x8D, 0x10)

    def poweron(self):
        self.cmd(0x8D, 0x14)
        self.cmd(0xAF)
        time.sleep_ms(100)

    def contrast(self, c):
        self.cmd(0x81, c & 0xFF)

    def invert(self, on):
        self.cmd(0xA7 if on else 0xA6)

    def show(self):
        self.cmd(0x21, 0, self.width - 1)   # column range
        self.cmd(0x22, 0, self.pages - 1)   # page range
        self.i2c.writeto(self.addr, b'\x40' + self.buffer)

example.code:
from machine import I2C, Pin
import time
from grove_oled_ssd1315 import SSD1315_I2C

i2c = I2C({I2C_ID}, sda=Pin({SDA}), scl=Pin({SCL}))
oled = SSD1315_I2C(i2c, addr=0x3C)
oled.fill(0)
oled.text('Grove OLED', 0, 0)
oled.text('SSD1315 ok', 0, 56)
oled.show()
print('OLED ready')
while True:
    time.sleep(1)
